BANKSY parameters

banksyParam.Rd

Parameters for GiottoClass::reduceData() that run BANKSY (Singhal et al. 2024) through the Bioconductor package Banksy: each cell's values are joined by the mean (and, with compute_agf = TRUE, the azimuthal gradient) of its spatial neighbours, weighted by lambda, and reduced by PCA. Banksy is suggested and checked when this runs.

Banksy takes the absolute value of the neighbour means, which is harmless for expression (never negative) but discards the sign of signed inputs such as PCs. Use expression as the input, or the native Giotto::runNeighborhoodPCA(), which keeps the sign.

If you use it, please cite the original paper (see References).

Usage

banksyParam(
  lambda = 0.8,
  k_geom = 15L,
  npcs = 20L,
  compute_agf = FALSE,
  seed = 1234L
)

# S4 method for class 'ANY,banksyParam'
reduceData(x, param, ..., spatial_locs)

Arguments

lambda

numeric in [0, 1], weight of the neighbourhood (about 0.8 for spatial domains, about 0.2 for cell typing)

k_geom

integer (or one per harmonic with compute_agf = TRUE), spatial neighbours

npcs

integer, principal components

compute_agf

logical, also use the azimuthal Gabor filter features

seed

integer, seed of the PCA

x

features x cells values with cell IDs as column names

param

a banksyParam

...

unused

spatial_locs

cells x 2 coordinates with cell IDs as row names

Value

A banksyParam object.

Details

reduceData(x, param, spatial_locs = ) returns a list with u (cells x npcs BANKSY PCs) and se, the SpatialExperiment Banksy worked on (for Banksy::clusterBanksy()).

References

Singhal V, Chou N, Lee J, et al. BANKSY unifies cell typing and tissue domain segmentation for scalable spatial omics data analysis. Nature Genetics 56, 431–441 (2024). doi:10.1038/s41588-024-01664-3

See also

runBanksy()

Examples

p <- banksyParam(lambda = 0.8)
